input.quote: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Commencing on the later of (i) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Binimetinib Product in the Ono Territory, or (ii) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Encorafenib Product in the Ono Territory, Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement, for any reasons by giving [ * ] advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination.
input.rationale: Section 13.2 gives Ono (our side) an at-will exit, but it does not arise until the later of two redacted periods measured from First Commercial Sale of each Product, so for a multi-year stretch of a term running to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term (13.1) we have no convenience right at all — walk-away territory under this rule — and the notice period itself is redacted rather than fixed at 30 days. There is also no pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts on such a termination. Array's side is acceptable: Article 13 gives Array only for-cause exits (13.3 material breach, 13.4 bankruptcy) plus the competing-product trigger in Section 8.2, so it has no convenience right during the committed term. The redline therefore makes the smallest change on our side only: it deletes the delayed commencement, fixes 30 days' written notice and adds the pro-rata refund, leaving the rationale requirement and all other termination mechanics untouched.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
mappings.quote: This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article 13, shall continue in full force and effect
mappings.explanation: Article 13 gives Array only for-cause termination rights (13.3 material breach, 13.4 bankruptcy), so it has no convenience exit.

proposal.summary: Make Ono's at-will termination right available immediately on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we must be able to exit for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. We have removed the delayed start tied to First Commercial Sale, fixed the notice period at thirty (30) days and added the pro-rata refund; Array retains no convenience exit under Article 13. If helpful, we can discuss 60-90 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.newText: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement at any time, for any reasons by giving thirty (30) days advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination. Array shall refund to Ono, on a pro rata basis, any fees prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination.
